<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/remote-transport.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`, `organization_id (literal, 35 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c3a8e07b6aca321c0114f49944b0564baf0d2c0f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `46e8fb2d681b86eb8ba0ef482e810adee61650b3` — the merge of head `5124ae06c29791dff42e5517d9838f2a096fd1b7` into base `c3a8e07b6aca321c0114f49944b0564baf0d2c0f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 46e8fb2d681b86eb8ba0ef482e810adee61650b3 && git checkout 46e8fb2d681b86eb8ba0ef482e810adee61650b3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c3a8e07b6aca321c0114f49944b0564baf0d2c0f 5124ae06c29791dff42e5517d9838f2a096fd1b7 && git checkout -B drift-repro c3a8e07b6aca321c0114f49944b0564baf0d2c0f && git merge --no-ff 5124ae06c29791dff42e5517d9838f2a096fd1b7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c3a8e07b6aca321c0114f49944b0564baf0d2c0f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c3a8e07b6aca321c0114f49944b0564baf0d2c0f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Method: the diff `307ce4c4b..2ee8e8d87` (19 files, +332/-241) read in a detached worktree at the head, the card #24583 and its claim (6284500102) and report (6286802345), ADR-0131 D1/D7/D8/D9/D14, the governing scripts, and the head's check runs over the GitHub API. Nothing built, run or re-run. Every measured number below (0 NULL rows on 35/66/30 tables, 14/172, suite counts, ablation) is the dev's; this record confirms the rule by code reading and the pins by reading the assertions.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. The arms — correct.** `SqlDriver.applyTenantScope` (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts:15587-15622`): the `group` path is `builder.whereIn(field, tenantIds.map(String))` at :15609 and the equality path is `builder.where(field, String(tenantId))` at :15621; neither `orWhereNull` remains, and the two exits (no tenant on the call :15592, no tenant field :15594) are untouched. A grep of `driver-sql/src` non-test code finds `whereNull`/`orWhereNull` only in the caller-authored `$null`/`$exists` filter lowering (:16640-16654), which is a predicate the caller wrote, not the scope. The Turso remote face follows by construction: `TursoDriver.remoteTenantScope` (`packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts:2538-2550`) hands `applyTenantScope` a bare builder and compiles whatever it added; `driver-turso/src` non-test code has no `IS NULL` on a tenant column; its two hunks (turso-driver.ts:2523-2524, remote-transport.ts:984) are docblocks. Posture: `computeTenantLayer0Verdict` (`packages/core/src/security/tenant-layer0-verdict.ts`, first line of the body) answers `none` whenever `postureEnforcesWall` is false, so under `single` `ObjectQL.driverReadScope` (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:7180-7215`) returns `undefined` and `buildDriverOptions` (engine.ts:7073-7125) threads no `tenantId`: the driver takes its first exit and no scope applies. Under `isolated` the verdict is `organization` and the predicate is exactly `organization_id = :t`; under `group` it is `organizations` and the predicate is `IN (...)`. The write target (`driverWriteTarget`, engine.ts:7222-7230, the one `writeTarget: true` site at engine.ts:16310) threads the active organization on inserts in every posture; those rows are stamped by `injectTenantOnInsert` (sql-driver.ts:15668-15680), so the insert read-back's union covers them (judgment 4). Anything else reading NULL organization rows THROUGH the driver's scope: none. What remains are explicit filters above the driver — `approval-service.ts:2761 businessUnitOrgScope`, `sharing-rule-service.ts:955 adminOrgScope` and `:1218` (the by-name NULL fallback), `organization-scope.ts:106-139 resolveOwnOrganizationRow`'s residue branch with its caller `delegated-admin-gate.ts:1294`, and `claim-orphan-org-rows.ts:94` (a system-context repair, unscoped by design). Under a wall the driver's equality now ANDs over each `$or`, so their NULL half is dead code; under `single` there is no driver scope and they read what they always read. They are 8c's "authz NULL readers" (step plan 6268559156 line 260 names `grantAppliesInTenant` and `criteriaContext`), another part of step 7, not this one — flagged in ③.

**2. The premise — holds by code reading.** (a) `single`: `LAYER0_NONE` means the arm was never reached with a tenant on any read door. (b) A composition that registers no organization object: `resolveSystemWriteOrganization` (`packages/core/src/security/system-write-organization.ts:86, :122`) answers `no-organization-object`; the engine's system-insert door (engine.ts:7427) and the share-link minter (`share-link-service.ts:763`) then return `undefined` and stamp nothing; the guest entry's organization step (`resolve-authz-context.ts`, `resolveGuestOrganization`, the D4 docblock at ~1215-1245) runs the same decision and resolves no organization; a session's `tenantId` is an active organization, which cannot exist without `sys_organization`, and with no AuthPlugin there is no session at all. So none of session, guest or system carries a tenant into `applyTenantScope` there; the arm was unreachable with a tenant, and its removal changes no answer. Known context (production `os serve`, no `OS_AUTH_SECRET`): `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts:4133-4166` — `resolvePlatformAuthComposition` does not compose, serve prints the yellow "AuthPlugin skipped — set OS_AUTH_SECRET to enable authentication in production" warning and continues; `serve.ts:4648` [#3963] denies anonymous object data unconditionally. On that boot the posture resolves `single` (and if the operator forced a wall, Layer 0 denies every data operation that carries no organization and the driver sees no tenant), so the driver carries no scope and every read and write is what it was before this PR; the boot still seeds NULL rows, which 7b-3 (6284744613, option A) is making a refusal. Confirmed: this PR alone changes nothing an operator sees on such a boot.

**3. The kept NULL disjunct — right call; it must not retire.** `sys_audit_log` declares `systemFields: { tenant: false }` (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-audit-log.object.ts:31`) and `tenant_id` as a plain `Field.lookup('sys_organization', { required: false })` (:398-402). `resolveTenantFieldName` (`packages/objectql/src/tenancy/system-write-organization.ts:198-213`) claims only a declared `tenancy.tenantField` or the injected `organization_id`; the ledger has neither, so it answers `null`, and the driver's twin `computeTenantField` honours the same opt-out, so `resolveTenantField('sys_audit_log')` is `null` and `applyTenantScope` exits before any predicate. `tenant_id` is therefore not a tenant column under D8; it is exactly D7's "plain attribution field under a name the tenant-field resolver does not claim, never the tenancy anchor". D1's "no nullable tenant column anywhere" does not reach a non-tenant column, and `check-tenant-chokepoint` scans only the two driver files (`scripts/check-tenant-chokepoint.mjs:124-126`), not the lifecycle service, so there is no gate conflict. The decision is made once: `tenantWindowsFor` (`packages/objectql/src/lifecycle/lifecycle-service.ts:1620-1639`) answers `nullIsLive: false` on `organization_id` (:1632) and `true` on an `ATTRIBUTION_PARTITION_COLUMNS` entry (:1636), and `globalPassSelector` (:272-276) is the only place that spells the `$or`. Retiring it would be wrong: with any tenant override on the ledger, a bare `$nin` on `tenant_id` never selects a deployment-level row (a value that is not there satisfies no positive comparison, #5298/#5299), so ADR-0057 retention would silently stop for exactly the rows the ledger exists to age out. The claim's literal "the `{ [column]: null }` disjunct goes" is correctly narrowed to the `organization_id` partition; the dev flagged the deviation (open question 2) — answered A in ③.

**4. The `readBackInsertedRows` guard — correct, minimal, within the part.** `sql-driver.ts:7635-7670`, guard at :7654-7659. `written` is the rows AFTER `injectTenantOnInsert` (create: :7508 then :7572; bulkCreate: :9857 then :9986), which fills every absent, null or empty tenant column when the call carries a tenant. Cases: (i) call with tenant → every row stamped → the union `IN (written)` scopes the read, the caller's `tenantIds` membership set replaced as before; (ii) call without tenant, every row explicitly stamped → the same union; (iii) call without tenant, mixed or unstamped rows → `{ ...options }`, no tenant, unscoped, bound by `whereIn(idColumn, written ids)`. A call with a tenant and an unstamped row cannot occur. Leak: none — in (iii) the read is bound to this call's own PRIMARY KEY ids, so it can answer only rows this call wrote, the same rows the old `IN (...) OR IS NULL` read answered. Miss: none — (iii) is the case the old arm served; it is now served by having no scope rather than a NULL arm, which is the D8-conformant shape. Without the guard, a no-tenant mixed `bulkCreate` on a dialect whose INSERT answers no rows would refuse (`insertedRowsNotReadBackError`) AFTER the write landed. The claim named this function's docblock; the guard is the same function's read-back consequence of the retired arm and the part is not complete without it — not a breach (open question 3, answered A). Pinned by the new #21227 case on both faces of that suite.

**5. Tests — every rewritten pin asserts the new rule; nothing weakened to green.** `sql-driver-tenant-scope.test.ts`: three reach pins become five (scoped `find` under org_a AND org_b with exact id sets, by-id `null`, count 2, scoped update and delete leave the row named `Orphan`, unscoped read still sees it); the union pin now passes `['org_a','org_b']` and asserts the full union minus g1 (nit: the update/delete pin swallows the call's result and asserts the stored row — the row is the fact). `sql-driver-tenant-scope-read-doors.test.ts`: p1 leaves every scoped expectation, an explicit `not.toContain('p1')` pin is added, and the unscoped window case still expects `['a1','a2','b1','b2','p1']` (:215-218) — both sides held. `sql-driver-21227-create-answers-stored-row.test.ts`: the new mixed-batch case asserts the returned pair and that `batch[1]` equals the stored row. `turso-local-remote-tenant-scope-parity.test.ts`: `orphan_1` moves from IN_SCOPE to OTHER_IDS, the aggregate sum drops the 1000, groups must not contain `null`; the both-faces-equal script inherits. `turso-remote-inherited-members.test.ts`: t3 re-stamped `org_c`, scoped `distinct` expects `['A']`; the NULL row there was incidental (the scoped-distinct rule is pinned in read-doors) and the remote-face refusal pin is unchanged. `tenant-audit-update-delete-half-repairs.test.ts`: the "legacy" row is now really organization-less (seeded with no tenant and `bypassTenantAudit`; the old seeding under `tenantId: 'org_A'` was stamped by inject, so the old "stays reachable" pin was vacuous — a correct finding, fixed in scope); the pin asserts scoped update and delete leave it `pending`; the walled D2 leg moves the reach assertions into a new pin that asserts `notFound` refusals and untouched rows. `rule-criteria-org-scope.test.ts`: `granted` is `['deal_a1']`, `not.toContain('deal_p1')`, `matchedRecords` 1; the platform-global rule's unscoped sweep is unchanged. `record-share-organization-stamp.test.ts`: the ORG_A rule grants deal_a1 only; the reconcile case flips from "aborts with RECORD_NOT_FOUND" to "completes", and the final set omits deal_a2 — the stale rule-B row IS revoked, so the pass now reaches its revoke loop: a stronger pin on designed behaviour. `share-link-organization-stamp.test.ts`: case 2 reaches the organization-less record through `{ isSystem: true }`, which is right because the service reads under the bare `SYSTEM_CTX` for system callers (`share-link-service.ts:72, :606`), a context with no tenant and so no driver scope; the new pin holds a session acting in ORG_B to `FORBIDDEN 403` with no row minted. Lifecycle (4 files): every `organization_id` partition expects the bare `$nin`; the `sys_audit_log` fixtures in `lifecycle-service.test.ts` are a test object WITH the column and are re-stamped (`org_plain`, and `other-200d` keeps the global-pass witness falsifiable); the attribution suite's helper branches by column, keeps the NULL arm on `tenant_id`, and its control "the ledger WITH the injected column partitions on it" expects the bare `$nin`.

**6. Clause-② and semver — `no (narrowing)` is right; `minor` with BREAKING is right.** Pure narrowing: the accept set of every tenant-scoped read door (find, count, aggregate, distinct, window read, update and delete predicates and their read-backs) shrinks by the organization-less rows, and the lifecycle global pass on `organization_id` shrinks the same way; the read-back guard changes no answer. Nothing widens: no export, type, error code or schema key is added or renamed (`TenantPartition.nullIsLive` is a non-exported interface field, `globalPassSelector` is module-private), so the claim line's `yes (the dev re-measures)` was correctly re-measured to `no (narrowing)` — `yes` is a widening of a published payload or accept set (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` header; `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs:244` fixes the spelling; `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs:156` maps it to this tier). Level: AGENTS.md:1088 — `(narrowing)` is BREAKING; ADR-0087 §launch-window as amended by #18003 — pre-GA a retirement ships `minor` carrying the BREAKING banner and an ADR-0087 disposition, and an npm `major` is never a side effect of one card; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` refuses `major`. The changeset carries `driver-sql: minor`, `objectql: minor`, the BREAKING banner, the `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker (correct: no key is removed), Before/Now/Unchanged, who is affected and the remedy (run the ceremony or stamp the row); driver-turso is correctly absent (docblocks only). Same shape as the 8b precedent `.changeset/15212-8b-walled-platform-insert-refused.md`. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

**7. Merge hygiene — this part alone.** `git merge-base origin/main 2ee8e8d87` is `307ce4c4b42503347d7f85825f572e4ca058b05f`; `git diff --stat 307ce4c4b...2ee8e8d87` equals `git diff --stat 307ce4c4b 2ee8e8d87` (19 files, +332/-241), so nothing from the base side rides in; `12d14765c` (#24681) is an ancestor of the head. The branch's own commits are `30473b42a..9987cf807` plus merges of the ceremony branch (`81ebc64bb`) and of main (`0012a4c6d`, `1f360ec75`, `2ee8e8d87`). `check-governed-merges` reports 0 of 19 on the register (dev), and no `docs/adr/**`, schema-differ, COALESCE or `__global__` path moves. `origin/main` has since advanced to `ddb3360a4` (55 files beyond the base); the claim's landing rule says the branch merges main again before it lands — see ③.

### ② Semver level

`minor` on `@objectstack/driver-sql` and `@objectstack/objectql`, BREAKING banner present, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` at the start of a line in both the PR body and the changeset, ADR-0087 disposition stated. Consistent with the diff (a read-scope narrowing, no removed or renamed authorable key, export or error code). Never `major`: correct under ADR-0087's level rule and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev open question 1 (Clause-②):** A — keep `no (narrowing)`, `minor`, BREAKING noted. The change narrows an accept set and widens nothing (judgment 6).
- **Dev open question 2 (lifecycle NULL disjunct):** A — keep it on the attribution partition only. `tenant_id` is not a tenant column (judgment 3); dropping it would strand deployment-level ledger rows whenever a tenant override exists.
- **Dev open question 3 (file surface):** A — accept. The additions are the pins that asserted the retired reach (plugin-sharing 3, service-storage 1, turso fixture re-stamp, #21227 case) and one same-function guard that the retired arm requires (judgment 4). No other runtime file moved; the Turso hunks are docblocks.
